podcast.body: This song was ranked #1 on a 2006 CNN poll of the worst songs of all time, winning "in a landslide." It reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in the summer of 1974. The song immediately faced significant backlash, particularly from the women's liberation movement, which criticized lyrics implying male ownership ("my baby" instead of "our baby") and presenting childbearing as a demonstration of a woman's love. Paul Anka, who wrote the song when his first wife Ann was pregnant, responded to the criticism in a San Francisco Examiner interview, stating, "To hell with what they think there are people out there who like to go to bed and have babies." Peter Riley, writing for Stereo Review in 1974, called it "the worst," criticizing Anka's "grunts out the unforgettable lyrics" and "Elvis-like roar," yet admitted he found himself "vacantly humming it" exactly as he did with "Diana" years prior, suggesting Anka possessed a "powerful natural gift of communication." Odia Coates sang along with Anka on the track. As an adult, the song appears to contain a subtle message regarding abortion, acknowledging it as a legal option with lyrics such as "you didn't have to do it wouldn't put you through it I swept it from your life but you wouldn't do it." The song also topped "more than one... worst of the 1970s poll and maybe the worst of all time."
